rule: Default post-PR watch is a fixed-default read biased to watching
description: P3 coupling. The post-PR watch is opt-out only, and what contains it is a BIAS, not determinism: one fixed default (`watch_requested`) and one admissible escape (`not_requested`), reachable only through an explicit no-watch instruction in the user's original request, read from the in-session request text, the only signal. The source pin sits on ONE span carrying BOTH halves of that conditional: the discriminating condition (`not_requested` holds if and only if the original request carries an explicit instruction not to watch or monitor the PR) and the obligation it triggers (every other case, including silence and ambiguity, yields `watch_requested`). Either half alone is rewritable while the other stays green -- deleting the `if and only if` keying re-opens the outcome to discretion, and inverting the default clause flips silence back to not-watching -- so both live inside the pinned span. Five further claim-carrying mechanisms in the same canonical file are pinned as separate entries, because the default rests on each of them: (a) the citation obligation, pinned as one span covering its trigger (taking `not_requested`), its destination (the verbatim span of the request relied on, named in the final report), and the fallback to `watch_requested` when no span can be cited -- any one of those three rewritten alone would hollow the obligation out, so they are pinned together, and a separate pin carries the in-session request text as the only signal; (b) the `HIVEMIND_SKIP_PR_WATCH` operator short-circuit, pinned as four short spans -- the named key, its presence-only test, its precedence over the request-text read, and the unset-or-empty complement that preserves the default -- so neither the escape nor its complement can be rewritten while the other stays green; (c) the Reflex site's POINTER, pinned in POINTER shape per rule 3 of the pin-authoring contract: the Reflex tail names the canonical `## Review Remediation Posture` predicate instead of restating it, and its own signal-and-citation clause (the in-session request text; the span named in the tail's own report) is pinned beside it, so severing the second site from the canonical rule, or dropping its signal difference, is loud; (d) the Engine site's POINTER, pinned in the same POINTER shape on text distinct from the Reflex pin so that neither pin can be satisfied by the other site: when a launched workflow's result carries `pr`, the Engine names the canonical `## Review Remediation Posture` predicate instead of restating it, and the one span carries both the `pr` trigger and the pointer, so severing the third site from the canonical rule, or detaching the pointer from its `pr` trigger, is loud; (e) the guide-run exemption, pinned as one span carrying both its condition (a guide run, as the Engine section defines it) and its obligation (it never watches, on any path), so deleting the exemption or rewriting its obligation into a watch is loud; the Engine hand-off and the Reflex tail name the exemption beside the `HIVEMIND_SKIP_PR_WATCH` short-circuit, and the node tests check those pointers and that the exemption sits in the Default post-PR watch paragraph. What this fixture honestly guarantees is exactly that these word sequences exist in this named file; it claims nothing about meaning and nothing about runtime behavior. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) the predicate is a NATURAL-LANGUAGE READ of untrusted prose, so no pin here can evaluate whether a given request is classified correctly -- the real containment is the bias toward `watch_requested`, and that bias protects against a hedging or uncertain read, which the ambiguity clause routes to watching, but NOT against a CONFIDENT LITERAL MISREAD, which can still reach `not_requested`; (2) the citation obligation is pinned as TEXT only -- a presence pin proves the obligation is still written down, never that the overlord actually names the relied-upon span in its final report at runtime; (3) a meaning-preserving rewrite-around is invisible -- surrounding prose that re-introduces overlord discretion while leaving the pinned bytes intact stays green; (4) the Reflex entries keep the pointer and the signal clause present and the Engine entry keeps its pointer present, but a presence pin cannot assert body-prose ABSENCE, so a second copy of the predicate growing back at any site is undetectable here; the node tests in `tests/workflow-scripts/overlord-contract.test.mjs` check that the Reflex section and the Engine pr hand-off paragraph do not restate it; (5) no fixture in this directory can detect a NEW decision state in a workflow that fails to carry the rule at all -- that is an absence defect per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract and needs a structural check, not a presence pin; (6) the guide-run pin proves presence only, never that the overlord recognizes a guide run at runtime, and the exemption keys on the exact line-1 text `hivemind-guide-run: <slug>`, so a guide launch whose first line differs is an ordinary request and is watched.

source.pattern: The outcome is `not_requested` if and only if the user's original request carries an explicit instruction not to watch or monitor the PR; in every other case, including silence and ambiguity, the outcome is `watch_requested`.

consumers.pattern: Taking `not_requested` obliges you to name the verbatim span of the request relied on in your final report; when no such span can be cited, the outcome is `watch_requested`.
`HIVEMIND_SKIP_PR_WATCH`, set in the project's `.claude/settings.json` `env` block, means never watch.
Check it by presence with a non-empty test
it takes precedence over the request-text read and short-circuits it
Unset or empty, the request-text read applies unchanged.
under the canonical predicate stated once under `## Review Remediation Posture` (Default post-PR watch)
The only signal is the in-session request text
The Reflex signal is the in-session request text, and the citation obligation is met by naming the relied-upon span in the tail's own report
when the result carries `pr`, apply the post-PR watch rule as written once in `## Review Remediation Posture` (Default post-PR watch)
A guide run, per `## Engine`, never watches on any path
